residue.text: Closest rival: a prescribed P2 schedule without live ledger handoff. Stage1 predicts co-presence matches transferred eight recognitions, whereas original and fallback bulk schedules yield three. Matching co-presence defeats the strong interaction claim: changed request choices alone can explain the gain. These are finite-model predictions, not execution evidence.

P1 alone predicts eight registrations and one initial recognition; P2 alone can recognize only the two initially registered notices. Their eligibility dependence remains. No available carrier moves this mandatory registration gate while preserving both parents; only informational coordination is transferable.

Burden: six validations and six dispatcher actions. Ledger reads add no clerk labor by stipulation, but no measured link-labor advantage is established. Extra capacity, configuration access and channels are unavailable. Delay origin and later sender adaptation remain unknown; no network trial or global-optimality proof supports coordination benefit.

summary.text: Keep eight registrations and eight distinct sender-recognized receipts by boundary 9 within six dispatcher actions. Six registrations and seven recognitions remain. The empty queue prevents tick-0 delivery; tick-8 requests cannot contribute.

Candidate: transfer completed-registration IDs and recognition/queue status from routine dashboard coordination to readable-ledger dispatch decisions. P1 validation and P2 request/delivery functions remain unchanged, using existing controls. Avoiding stale N1 and already queued identities is a hypothesis; registration eligibility remains mandatory.

Validate N3 through N8 at ticks 0 through 5. Individually request N2,N3,N4 at 0,1,2; bulk at 4 queues N5,N6; individually request N7 at 5 and N8 at 6. Predicted deliveries: N2,N3,N4 at 1,2,3; N5,N6,N7,N8 at 5,6,7,8. Six actions; N8 delivers while available.

Compare original dashboard bulk requests at 0,1,2,4,5,6; transferred schedule; broken informational handoff with original fallback; co-presence with schedule prescribed; and each parent alone, holding validation order fixed where present. Measure registrations, distinct recognitions, actions and queue waste. Interaction predicts matched-control handoff ablation lowers recognition; control-only rival predicts prescribed co-presence matches transfer. Fallback changes controls, so it alone cannot separate these explanations.
